content.title: About
content.content: Meatless lasagna is a layered Italian dish made with pasta sheets, tomato sauce, plant‑based mince, cheese and spices. It contains no animal protein but retains the classic taste and aroma of traditional lasagna.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetarian lasagna often replaces meat with soy mince, mushrooms or lentils, boosting plant protein content.
The classic lasagna recipe originated in the Mediterranean in the 19th century; vegetarian versions appeared in the 1970s with the rise of plant‑based cuisine.
Pasta sheets can be made from whole‑grain flour, increasing fiber levels.
Cheese is sometimes swapped for vegan alternatives made from nuts or soy protein.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Soy mince, lentils or mushrooms provide complete amino acids for muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain pasta and vegetable additions support digestion and blood‑sugar stability.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Absence of meat and use of plant oils make the dish heart‑friendly.

items.title: Abundant vitamins and minerals
items.content: Tomatoes, spinach and other veggies supply vitamin C, potassium, iron and folate.

items.title: Supports gut health
items.content: Fiber and prebiotics from vegetables promote beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Soy‑based mince can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and vegan cheeses often contain high salt levels; check labels.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional pasta contains gluten; use gluten‑free alternatives for celiac disease.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Boil pasta sheets until al dente, prepare a sauce with tomatoes, plant mince, onion, garlic and spices. In a baking dish layer pasta, sauce, vegan cheese, repeat. Bake at 180 °C for 30‑35 minutes until golden. Let rest 10 minutes before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked lasagna in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Freeze individual portions for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.
